RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the October 21, 2008/Asvina 29, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Corporate Affairs; Culture; Finance; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Tourism; Water Resources )
Total number of questions — 20
15
Small Savings Schemes
†*41. SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the deposits
in small savings schemes being run through
post offices have reduced due to reduction
in interest rates during the last few years;
(b) whether it is also a fact that interest
rates being offered by banks are higher;
(c) if so, whether Government is
considering to make the interest rate of small
savings schemes equal to those of the banks;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
CNG filling stations in NCR
  *42. SHRI HARISH RAW A T:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Indraprastha Gas Limited
(IGL) has failed to provide adequate
number of CNG filling stations in the
National Capital and NCR towns resulting
in inconvenience to CNG vehicle owners;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether CNG vehicle owners have
to wait hours together to get fuel from the
CNG stations; and
(d) if so, the steps taken by Government
to set up more CNG stations in  the
National Capital and NCR towns and also
to increase the filling capacity of the existing
CNG stations?
LPG supply to Northern States
*43. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) the monthly requirement of LPG in
each State, district-wise;
(b) the quantity of LPG supplied to
each State during each of the last two years
and the first eight months of the current
year, State-wise, district-wise;
(c) whether Government is aware that
there is an acute shortage of LPG in many
States, especially Uttar Pradesh;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

16
(d) if so, whether Government has
received requests from various States
particularly Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand,
Madhya Pradesh and Punjab for increasing
the quotas of LPG in their States;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) the action taken by Government
thereon?
Appointment of Judicial Commission
on Kosi Floods
*44. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of W ATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal under
Government's consideration to appoint a
high power judicial commission to go  into
the circumstances that led to breach of dam
and embankment of river Kosi in the
Nepalese territory, which caused
unprecedented floods in Bihar inundating
large areas in the State;
(b) if so, the composition thereof, the
terms of reference and time to be allowed
to the Commission to submit its report;
and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
New Civil Aviation Policy
*45. SHRI RAMDAS AGARW AL:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIA TION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has decided to
notify its new Civil Aviation Policy;
(b) if so, how much time it is likely to
take to facilitate creation of proposed 500
Mega and 6 Regional Airports as well as to
develop mechanism for aviation grid for
setting up of multi-modal merchant airports;
(c) what steps Government has taken
to make its 100 airports operational, whose
number at present is only 50; and
(d) whether new policy would have
provisions for making 100 aerotropolis in
10 major metros and also establish air
linkages for air passengers for minimum of
50 kms. of distance?
'Adopt a Monument' scheme in
Rajasthan
†*46. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether heritage sites in Rajasthan
are being given to private sectors for their
renovation and maintenance under "Adopt
a Monument" scheme;
(b) if so, the extent to which this scheme
has been successful; and
(c) whether the Government of India
would consider to give archaeological
buildings under this scheme?
Promotion of river tourism in
Andhra Pradesh
*47. SHRI M.V . MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased
to state:
(a) the details of riverine tourism
promoted in the State of Andhra Pradesh;
(b) whether any financial assistance is
extended by the Ministry for promotion
of riverine tourism in Andhra Pradesh; and
(c) if so, the details thereof during the
last three years, year-wise and project-wise?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

17
Minutes of Meetings of EGOM
*48. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that copies of the
minutes of meeting of the Empowered
Group of Ministers (EGOM) have been
sent to private companies like RIL and
NIKO Ltd.;
(b) if so, the details thereof including
other papers sent to those companies since
January, 2007 till date;
(c) whether it is also a fact that these
papers are confidential in nature and if so,
under which rule such papers have been
sent to private companies;
(d) whether Government has fixed any
responsibility on the officer concerned who
have been sending such papers to private
companies; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Promotion of Sattra Institutions in Assam
*49. SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD
BAISHYA: Will the Minister of
CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government of India
has received a proposal from the State
Government of Assam for assistance to
Sattra (Vaishnava Monasteries) Institutions
of Assam for promotion of their art forms
as well as for improvement of basic
infrastructure and preservation of heritage
properties;
(b) if so, the details of the proposal and
its present status of sanction, total outlay
and allocation made, year-wise; and
(c) if not, whether Government has
taken any programme for fulfilling those
objectives?
Fixation of pay
*50. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) the rationale for fixing the fitment
multiplication factor at 1.86 for fixation of
pay after sixth Pay Commission;
(b) whether this multiplication factor is
being reviewed for certain scientific
organizations;
(c) whether there is any proposal/
demand to enhance this multiplication factor
to 2.25 from 1.86 in case of employees
under the Department of Atomic Energy
and the Department of Space;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) if not, the reasons therefor;
(f) by when a decision in this regard is
likely to be taken; and
(g) whether Departments like Atomic
Energy, Space, Defence Research and
Development Organisation (DRDO),
Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
(CSIR) have been given flexibility to
enhance this fitment factor in order to retain/
attract scientific talent?
Forex derivatives losses
*51. DR. (SHRIMA TI) NAJMA A.
HEPTULLA:
SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that forex
derivatives losses may well turn out to be
the subprime crisis for India Inc.;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the size
of the potential Market-to-Market
(MTM) losses at corporates is placed
anywhere around Rs. 120-200 billion;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether the exposure of banks
operating in India, including foreign banks

18
to derivatives grew 291 per cent in two
years to reach Rs. 127.86 trillion by the
end of 2007; and
(e) if so, the measures taken in this
regard?
Increase in gas prices from KG Basin
*52. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is considering
a revision of gas price of Reliance Industries
Ltd. (RIL) as and when the gas is available
from its KG Basin;
(b) whether the RIL is lending pressure
on Government to raise the gas price at
4.20 dollars per unit based on global crude
price of 60 dollars per barrel;
(c) whether ONGC is supplying gas at
a price of 2.2 dollars per unit; and
(d) if so, what is the basis of RIL's
demand for raising gas price at 4.20 dollars
per unit?
Credit cards
*53. SHRI JAI PRAKASH
NARAYAN SINGH: Will the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether RBI has been receiving large
number of complaints against Indian and
foreign banks concerning credit cards;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether banks are issuing credit
cards suo moto and thereafter harass
individuals to pay charges etc.; and
(d) the steps taken to curb such
fraudulent practices of banks?
Commissioning of Iran-Pakistan-
India Gas Pipeline Project
*54. SHRI R.C. SINGH:
SHRI D. RAJA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS  be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the talks on
the proposed Iran-Pakistan-India Gas
Pipeline Project have been progressing very
slowly;
(b) if so, at what stage the talks are and
what are the issues remaining to be solved;
and
(c) what steps are being taken for the
early commissioning of the project?
India as a preferred Business
Destination
*55. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI VIJAY JAWAHARLAL
DARDA:
Will the Minister of CORPORATE
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether a FORBES study,
containing a comparative business analysis
from various angles in 121 countries, has
ascribed India's fall in ranking this year from
51st to 64th to "demonstrated resistance
to increasing personal freedom, higher
inflation from food and other commodity
costs, as well as increased burdens on
entrepreneurs, etc."; and
(b) if so, what steps Government
proposes to take so that India becomes a
preferred "Business Destination" in the fast
emerging global market?
Increasing supply of dollars
*56. SHRIMATI T. RA TNA BAI: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the RBI has announced a
package of measures aimed at increasing
the supply of dollars and augmenting
liquidity;

19
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
exchange rate is primarily determined by
demand and supply and the outflow of
portfolio capital aggravated the rupee's fall;
and
(d) if so, the response of Government
thereon?
Revival of PSEs
*57. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of HEA VY INDUSTRIES AND
PUBLIC ENTERPRISES be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of unviable Public Sector
Enterprises (PSEs) registered with the
Board of Industrial and Financial
Reconstruction (BIFR) upto September,
2008, PSE-wise and location-wise; and
(b) the steps taken to revive them?
Compensation to oil companies
*58. SHRI V . HANUMANTHA
RAO:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether he has met the Finance
Minister to seek more compensation for
oil companies incurring huge losses on fuel
sales;
(b) if so, whether the Indian basket of
crude oil average $99.76 per barrel in March
which averaged $96.73 per barrel in
2007-08;
(c) if so, what was the outcome of the
discussions held; and
(d) to what extent the Finance Ministry
has agreed to provide compensation to oil
companies?
Merger of State Bank of Saurashtra
with SBI
*59. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
SHRI D. RAJA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has approved
the merger of State Bank of Saurashtra with
State Bank of India (SBI);
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) whether the trade unions in the
Banking Sector have opposed the merging
of subsidiary banks with SBI; and
(d) if so, what are the main concerns of
the trade unions and Government's reaction
thereto?
Wealth of big companies
*60. SHRI MA TILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) the names of the ten largest corporate
establishments of the country and the value
of wealth owned by them, corporate-wise;
(b) the amount of money invested in
the country by foreign corporate
establishments, name-wise and amount-
wise;
(c) how this accumulation of wealth
becomes a cause for inflation; and
(d) the remedial measures proposed?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 15th October, 2008 Secretary-General.
Asvina 23, 1930 (Saka)

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Civil Aviation : 45,
Corporate Affairs : 55, 60,
Culture : 46, 49,
Finance : 41, 50, 51, 53, 56, 59,
Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises : 57,
Petroleum and Natural Gas : 42, 43, 48, 52, 54, 58,
Tourism : 47,
Water Resources : 44.
